title: Lower tail vanishing for bounded complexes
statement:
Let $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$, $C\in\Cons(X,\Lambda)$, and let $L\in\Dic(X,\Lambda)$ be bounded with
$H^q(L)=0$ for $q>-d_C-1$. Then $\Hom(C,L)=0$.

Here $X$ is a scheme, the coefficients are the condensed coefficient rings of
[sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], pulled back to $\Lambda_X$ as in
[sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]; $\Mod(\Lambda_X)$ is the module-object category
of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], and $\Cons$ is the category of constructible
$\Lambda_X$-modules [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. The integer $d_C\geq0$ is a chosen
uniform bound from [sk-lem-uniform-constructible-ext]:
$\Ext^r(C,N)=0$ for every constructible $N$ and every $r>d_C$.
Write $\IndCons(X,\Lambda)$ for the sheaves isomorphic to small filtered colimits
of constructible sheaves, and define $\Dic(X,\Lambda)$ to be the full subcategory
of $D(\Mod(\Lambda_X))$ on objects whose cohomology sheaves all belong to
$\IndCons(X,\Lambda)$. The derived category and cohomology are those of
[def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Bounded means that only finitely many
cohomology sheaves are nonzero; $C$ is placed in degree zero and
$\Hom(C,L)$ means morphisms in this ambient derived category, with the shift
and Ext conventions of [def-pc-ext].

proof.text: Put S=C[0] and Q(M)=Subsingleton Hom(S,M). Postcomposition with an isomorphism is injective, so Q is replete. Zero objects satisfy Q. For a distinguished triangle A -> M -> B, if Q(A) and Q(B), every map S -> M has zero composite to B and factors through A by [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact]; the factor is zero. Thus Q is closed under extensions.

proof.text: Use the proved source-library theorem DerivedCategory.prop_of_bounded_of_degreewise (WeilConjectures.Mathlib.Algebra.Homology.DerivedCategory.TStructure), with P(q,N)=Q(N placed in degree q). This theorem implements the canonical truncation induction using the standard t-structure [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category] and the concentration-in-one-degree lemma [lem-sf-derived-concentrated-single]. Finite cohomology support is bounded above and below; isGE_iff and isLE_iff therefore supply its boundedness input, including empty support. P(q,-) is replete by applying the single functor to isomorphisms.

proof.text: For each q > -d_C-1, H^q(L) is zero, and its single complex is zero. Otherwise set r=(-q).toNat. Since d_C is nonnegative and q <= -d_C-1, r is a natural number with r=-q in Z and d_C<r. Apply [lem-finite-window-ind-ext-bound] to H^q(L), which is ind-constructible by hL, using the very same constructible Ext bound hExt. The coefficient equality in that lemma is equality of bundled monoid objects and hence retains the specified multiplication. For algebraic-closure coefficients choose the actual bottom finite intermediate field; no witness is selected from an unproved existence theorem.

source.place: bounded-complex truncation induction and one-cohomology case

proof.text: By [def-pc-ext], Ext.homEquiv identifies the vanishing Ext group with Hom(C[0],H^q(L)[r]). The source-library singleFunctors.shiftIso identifies the shifted single complex with the sheaf placed in degree q. This gives P(q,H^q(L)) at every q. The degreewise induction in step 2 now gives Q(L), exactly the unchanged conclusion for both coefficient choices.
